subject: FinCentric DPA route & SCC module — controller/processor confirmation
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fencentric.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-07T15:08:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap + GDPR routing question

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion. As a quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- SOC 2: we confirmed Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for hosted and Dedicated; we can share the attestation once NDA/LOI is in place.
- GDPR: you asked about DPA pathing and SCC module options — we need to confirm whether FinCentric will act as a controller for user data processed by your product, or whether Redwood will be a processor for FinCentric's customer data.
- HIPAA: noted as a potential future scope; Redwood offers BAAs for Private deployments — we can scope that separately.

Action items I propose: 1) please confirm controller vs processor for the FinCentric use case, 2) if controller, decide whether you want the standard EU SCC module (controller-controller) or controller-processor flow with our DPA + SCC clauses, and 3) I'll attach a redlineable DPA + a short SCC comparison matrix to make the choice easier.

Attaching a draft DPA and a short matrix for your legal team to review. If it helps, we can schedule a quick call with our legal ops (Laura) to walk through the options.

Cheers,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: scc-module-comparison.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fencentric.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@fencentric.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + GDPR routing question

Thanks Jonas — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Controller/Processor: For the initial integration FinCentric will remain the controller for customer telemetry and PII; Redwood will be a processor for the inference-related artefacts we send.
- SCC module: Legal prefers the controller-processor SCC path (so we can stick with the standard Processor Addendum).
- SOC 2: we will need the attestation and a short evidence pack (data segregation, logging, retention policy).

Could you loop in your legal ops and share the DPA redlineable copy and the SCC comparison in a single place? Also we prefer to complete a VSQ first (we use a vendor questionnaire template). I'll send you the questionnaire today so you can estimate completion time.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal & Privacy, FinCentric

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fencentric.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-08T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + GDPR routing question

Hi Elena — thanks for confirming. 

We've updated the DPA to assume Redwood as processor and included the controller-processor SCC module variant. Key notes included in redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf: 
- Purpose-limited processing and documented subprocessor list
- Retention and deletion timelines tied to your retention policy
- Incident notification SLA and forensics access (48 hours notice window)

I've also added an SCC matrix (scc-module-comparison.xlsx) with recommended routing for EU vs non-EU data and our suggested clauses for processor scenarios. Laura (cc) will take point on the evidence pack for SOC 2. 

Next steps: 
1) Elena / FinCentric to confirm the controller-processor route formally (short email OK) so legal can start redlines.
2) FinCentric to send the VSQ (vendor security questionnaire). Once received, we aim to return a first-pass response within 5 business days.
3) Laura will attach the SOC 2 attestation + the data retention and logging snapshot in a shared Drive link.

If that aligns, I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-min legal touchpoint tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas
[Attachment: redwood_DPA_draft_v2.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: scc-module-comparison.xlsx (Excel)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fencentric.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@fencentric.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-09T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + GDPR routing question — next steps and VSQ kickoff

Hi Elena / Tom —

Looping in from Legal Ops — glad to see the controller/processor path is preferred, that simplifies the DPA route. Quick practical notes from our side: 

- VSQ: thanks for sharing — we've started filling the questionnaire. To avoid back-and-forth, I attached a short checklist of items we'll likely need: (1) SOC 2 report, (2) list of subprocessors, (3) data flow diagram showing where inference requests and logs are stored, (4) retention policy excerpt. 
- Attestations & evidence: I posted the SOC 2 bridge letter and scope snapshot to the Drive folder (see link above). If you want a redline session on the DPA, I can host an hour tomorrow at 10:00 CET.
- SCC module: we recommend the controller-processor SCC module with the processor addendum attached; if FinCentric needs controller-controller language for any EU-to-EU cross-processing, note that creates additional obligations (we flagged those in the matrix).

Please confirm the VSQ location or paste the questionnaire link and I'll assign owners internally. Looking forward to closing the contracting gate quickly.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vsq-checklist.txt (text)]
